Hi Anil — thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary up front: we can provide a per-environment csv snapshot that maps IP ranges to services (control plane, runtime egress, telemetry, package updates). Attachments below include the CSV snapshot and a short evidence PDF that describes IP rotation policy and our TLS behavior.

A few clarifying notes:
- For Private deployments we operate a control plane that communicates with the customer VPC over the private endpoint; runtime outbound traffic (model weights updates, container registry pulls, telemetry) originates from a small set of egress ranges. Some customers request NAT with static IPs, others accept our managed egress pool.
- Prod ranges are stable for SLA customers (reserved pools) and we offer an SLA addendum for static binding; dev/stage can be ephemeral unless you request reserved binding.
- Typical ports: 443 (HTTPS) for all services; 853/53 only if DNS proxying is requested (most customers do not require explicit DNS allowlisting).

- harrington-egress-list.csv (snapshot as requested)
- redwood-egress-evidence.pdf (attestation + rotation cadence)

If you need formal attestation language for procurement, we can produce a one-paragraph SOC2-friendly statement.

Best,

Anil — looping in a few implementation details and the proposed firewall rule set for your infra team to review. I also attach an abbreviated runbook for validation and an example permitlist that aligns to the CSV.

Proposed minimal allowlist (prod):
- 13.59.100.0/24 — control-plane-api.redwood-inference.com — TCP 443 — reason: control plane API traffic (verify TLS SNI)
- 54.221.200.128/26 — runtime-egress-us-west-2 — TCP 443 — reason: model artifact fetches + container registry pulls
- 34.210.45.0/27 — telemetry.redwood-ops.net — TCP 443 — reason: anonymized usage telemetry (opt-out available)

Notes and caveats:
- If Harrington requires immutable egress IPs for prod we can bind a reserved NAT pool; that requires a 30-day lead and SLA addendum.
- Dev/stage CSV rows are marked as ephemeral; if you need bindings for those environments we can promote specific pools.
- We recommend not allowlisting DNS responses (53) unless you require outbound DNS to our proxies; instead prefer outbound HTTPS to the listed FQDNs.

Validation runbook (short):
1) Apply rules in non-prod and run a synthetic job that pulls a small model artifact (provided test artifact).
2) Capture tcpdump on egress and confirm destination IPs map to the CSV snapshot.
3) Verify TLS SNI equals expected FQDN in 100% of checks.
4) For prod, request reserved NAT binding and schedule a maintenance window for final cutover.

I'll prepare a redlined one-paragraph attestation for procurement if you confirm language.

—Marissa
Customer Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
